verifications.claim: As of March 2026, the Biden administration's Saving on a Valuable Education (SAVE) plan is effectively terminated following court orders.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'court officially terminated'; R5: 'Biden’s Save student loan plan is officially dead' (Mar 27, 2026); R6: 'A federal judge recently approved a settlement... to eliminate SAVE altogether' (Mar 27, 2026); R1: 'currently blocked by the courts'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources dated March 2026 confirm termination due to court actions and settlements.

verifications.claim: Seven million+ borrowers must switch from SAVE to other repayment plans.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'More than 7.5 million borrowers'; R5: 'more than 7 million people in the Saving on a Valuable Education plan'; R6: '7 million borrowers enrolled in the SAVE plan'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state 7+ million must switch plans.

verifications.claim: The SAVE plan offered 5% discretionary income payments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Require borrowers to pay no more than 5% of their discretionary income monthly on undergraduate loans'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to SAVE plan features.

verifications.claim: The SAVE plan offered fast forgiveness.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R5: 'a faster path to loan forgiveness than other income-driven repayment plans'; R2: 'Forgive loan balances after 10 years of payments, instead of 20 years, for borrowers with loan balances of $12,000 or less'
verifications.reasoning: 'Fast' is subjective but supported by descriptions of shorter timelines vs. other plans.

verifications.claim: SAVE borrowers have a 90-day window to switch to a legal plan.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'they have 90 days to switch out of the SAVE Plan'; R6: 'they have 90 days to select a new repayment plan'

verifications.claim: The Department of Education is introducing a Repayment Assistance Plan with 30-year relief terms.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'new Repayment Assistance Plan... allows for relief after 30 years'; R4: 'new Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP)'

verifications.claim: The Department of Education is introducing a Tiered Standard Plan.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'the new Tiered Standard Plan... timelines between 10 years and 25 years to repay'

verifications.claim: The SAVE plan covered unpaid monthly interest so balances did not grow.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Cover the borrower's unpaid monthly interest, so that... no borrower's loan balance will grow as long as they make their monthly payments—even when that monthly payment is $0'
verifications.reasoning: Exact feature of SAVE plan described.

verifications.claim: The SAVE plan reduced monthly payments to $0 for low-income borrowers under 225% of the poverty line.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'guaranteeing that no borrower earning under 225% of the federal poverty level... will have to make a monthly payment'

verifications.claim: The SAVE plan reduced monthly payments to 5% of discretionary income for undergraduates.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Require borrowers to pay no more than 5% of their discretionary income monthly on undergraduate loans'

verifications.claim: Enrolled SAVE borrowers were placed in interest-free forbearance while legal challenges occurred.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Borrowers enrolled in the SAVE plan have been placed in a forbearance... But the Department has started charging interest on these loans again, since August 1, 2025, so borrowers... will see their student loan balances increase'
verifications.reasoning: Forbearance explicitly includes interest accrual, contradicting 'interest-free'.

verifications.claim: Large-scale student debt cancellation initiatives were largely struck down by the Supreme Court in 2023.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the U.S. Supreme Court striking down the president’s plan in a 6-3 decision' (June 2023); 'Supreme Court blocked the debt forgiveness plan in a 6-3 decision'
verifications.reasoning: Direct reference to SCOTUS striking down Biden's broad cancellation plan in 2023.
